setting.help: Turn validated transfers into EPCIS events: a receipt, a transfer, a pack, a delivery. Master data says what a product is; these say what became of one of them.

div.div: The EPCIS repository is a different service from the resolver, and usually a different host. The credential is the same offline token — but capture is a separate permission, and a token that publishes master data can still be refused here.
Only for logistic units. An SSCC is the one GS1 key a company issues by itself — no registry is involved — and a pallet needs one before it can say what is underneath it.

setting.help: The repository holds more than our own events: it is where a chain meets. Reading it back is how Odoo learns what happened to a pallet after it left the yard.

div.div: Narrowing is a convenience, not a permission — the repository already decides what this credential may see at all. It only decides how much of that ends up in the inbox.

The two limits bound a single run, not the total. Whatever a run does not reach stays behind the watermark and is read next time, so a connector that has been off for a day catches up in steps instead of in one long transaction.
Whether an incoming event may post anything is not set here: it is set per operation type, and allowed per partner. Both have to agree, and neither can make an event create a document or stock.
